files.privacyShort: Once published, anyone can read it and it cannot be deleted.
files.hintSyncTitle: "Sync to registry" registers the file into your on-chain registry (a small registration fee per file, about 10% of the storage fee with a 0.01 AI3 floor); on a new device, connect the same wallet and click "Recover from registry" to restore the file list.
files.hintSyncBody: Registering is optional — the file itself can always be fetched for free with its manifest or by scanning the chain. A manifest is a self-contained retrieval credential (it locates every data block); export it and any device can use it. Cost comparison on the About page.
files.empty: No files yet. Upload, import a manifest, or recover from the on-chain registry.
files.privacyRegistry: The on-chain registry holds your file list — connect the same wallet on a new device to recover it in one click.
files.hintRegistry: The registry is a public index (which wallet registered which files), not access control: published data itself is readable by anyone. Registration charges a dev fee (≈10% of the on-chain storage fee, 0.01 AI3 floor) that funds the maintenance of the public frontend and tooling; skipping registration does not affect retrieving the data itself from the chain.

files.encryptToggleHint: Content is encrypted with AES-256-GCM before upload. The file key is wrapped with your wallet signature (deterministic wallets) and optionally a passphrase — the same wallet (or the passphrase) decrypts on download. Filename and size stay public; others can retrieve the ciphertext but cannot read it.

vault.title: Vault
vault.needEvm: Vaults are namespaced by EVM address — connect an EVM signer first (extension wallet or local key) in the header.
vault.createIntro: Entries are encrypted before they go on-chain permanently (only ciphertext ever reaches the chain). Set a recovery passphrase:
vault.createHint: In brief: a random data key encrypts all entries, and the key itself is wrapped by two independent channels — your passphrase and your wallet signature. Everyday unlocking is just a wallet signature; if the wallet is lost, the keystore file + passphrase recover everything. Full principles and do-it-yourself verification:
vault.passphraseLabel: Recovery passphrase (≥8 chars, encrypts the keystore file)
vault.passShort: ✗ passphrase needs at least 8 characters (it encrypts the keystore file; without it the keystore is just a file)
vault.generating: generating the data key and envelope…
vault.signingBind: wallet signature (binds the unlock channel to this wallet; may be declined)…
vault.createdLocal: ✓ vault created (locally). "Save on-chain" after adding entries creates the on-chain versions.
vault.keystoreWarning: This file is the only recovery path if the wallet is lost — store it offline and carefully (it is already encrypted under your passphrase; a leaked file does not leak entries).
vault.keystoreSaved: I have stored it safely (losing it leaves only the wallet-signature unlock)
vault.lockedIntro: Unlock with one EVM wallet signature — no passphrase, no transaction.
vault.keystoreFallbackIntro: If the wallet is unavailable (new wallet / some extension wallets sign non-reproducibly), unlock with the keystore file exported at creation + your passphrase:
vault.noSignatureChannel: this envelope has no signature channel bound to this wallet, or the wallet signature is not reproducible — use the keystore file instead
vault.privacyMemory: Entries live only in this page's memory (locked on refresh); only ciphertext goes on-chain.
vault.hintEncryption: Encryption happens in your browser: a random data key encrypts all entries, and the key — wrapped by your passphrase/wallet signature — is published alongside the ciphertext. Nobody (including us) can read the entries from the on-chain data alone.

about.feeIntro: PermaDrive publishes at the protocol level: what you pay is what you store, and the data is kept **permanently**. The official AutoDrive service prices storage in credits (expiring after 90 days, purchase requires a Google login). Both PermaDrive fees below are read live from the chain (consensus storage fee + FileRegistry quote); the official price is the 2026-10 measured figure.
about.connectingRates: Connecting to the consensus chain for live rates…
about.feeFormula: max(minFee, size × feePerByte) — overpayment is refunded automatically
about.paramsValue: feePerByte {0} wei/byte · minFee {1} AI3 · cap {2} AI3/byte (hard anti-rug ceiling)
about.sovereigntyNote: The dev fee is charged on the value-added point of one-click cross-device recovery; not registering leaves the data itself untouched — files can always be fetched for free with their manifest or by scanning the chain directly (no involvement of this project). Registration fees go straight to the project treasury and fund the maintenance of the public frontend and tooling.
about.featureFilesDesc: Any file packed as IPLD and published on-chain, archived permanently by the farmer network; the manifest is the retrieval credential
about.featureNotesDesc: Append-only text records; every save is a new immutable version, the version chain is held in the on-chain registry
about.featureNotesCost: per version: storage fee + dev fee (small texts usually hit the 0.01 AI3 floor)
about.featureVaultDesc: Entries are AES-256-GCM encrypted as one envelope before publishing (only ciphertext reaches the chain); one wallet-signature unlock, keystore file as the recovery fallback
about.featureVaultCost: per save: storage fee + dev fee (you control the registration cadence)
about.plaintextNote: "My files" and notes are published in the clear (permanently public); private text belongs in the encrypted vault — principles and do-it-yourself verification in
about.sovAccountsDesc: wallet signatures are the identity; no personal information is collected
about.sovBackendDesc: fully static frontend; the RPC / indexer dependencies are replaceable public protocol infrastructure
about.sovLockInDesc: manifests are self-contained and shareable; even if this project disappears, any public infrastructure can still retrieve your data in full
about.sovPermanentDesc: published data cannot be deleted (that is what makes version history and undelete possible) — make sure content is fit for public before publishing

settings.networkIntro: Manifests only record the network identifier (mainnet); endpoints are this app's configuration — switching endpoints does not affect retrieving existing files. Public RPC endpoints rate-limit; the default minimum interval between consecutive requests is ≥1.6s.

messages.title: On-chain Private Messages
messages.encryptNotice: Messages are end-to-end encrypted (x25519-xsalsa20-poly1305). Who talks to whom, when, and ciphertext length are public — only the content is private.
messages.connectFirst: Connect a wallet to use messages. Receiving must be enabled once (Messages page → Enable receiving), which announces your encryption key on-chain.
messages.empty: No conversations yet. Send a message to any address that has announced an encryption key.
messages.pickConversation: Pick a conversation on the left, or start a new one.

messages.locked: 🔒 encrypted (connect the same wallet to decrypt)
messages.noPlainSelf: 🔒 sent from another device (outbox plaintext is local-only)
messages.enableExplain: Enable private messages and paid-file key delivery: the wallet will first request your encryption public key (no gas). If registration is needed, a separate Auto-EVM transaction publishes this public key and costs gas. Your private key is not published.
messages.sendExplain: Send an encrypted message on Auto-EVM. This transaction costs gas; recipient, sender and message time are public. Continue?

paywall.title: Paid downloads
paywall.notice: Digital-goods mode: buying grants the file itself (no DRM). Payment is held in escrow and released on your confirmation; refundable automatically if the seller never delivers (timeout) or within the grace period after delivery. The file key is delivered via an end-to-end encrypted message; delivery is semi-automatic (the seller's app responds when online). Only encrypted files make sense to sell.
paywall.connectFirst: Connect a wallet to use paid downloads.
paywall.enableReceivingFirst: Enable receiving first (Messages page → Enable receiving) — otherwise the seller cannot deliver the file key and the order would only be refundable after the timeout.
paywall.selectHint: Encrypted files only — a buyer receives the file key after payment.
paywall.pendingEmpty: No pending paid requests. Purchases of your listed files appear here for key delivery.
paywall.delivering: Delivering key to {0} (sign + encrypted message + markDelivered)…
paywall.viewEmpty: No registry entries for this address.
paywall.purchasedOk: Purchased "{0}" for {1} AI3 — waiting for key delivery.
paywall.waitingDelivery: Key not delivered yet — the seller's app delivers when online. Check again later.
paywall.legacyFrozenNotice: The paywall v1 contract is frozen (security review): new listings, purchases and deliveries are disabled. Existing orders keep refund / confirm / withdraw.
paywall.legacyListFrozen: Listing is disabled while the v1 contract is frozen — available after PaywallV2 deployment.
paywall.legacyConfirmRisk: Legacy orders settle to the CURRENT listing seller on the frozen v1 contract. The pre-confirm check cannot fully rule out an overwrite between the check and the transaction (TOCTOU) — for high-value orders, refund is the safer option.
paywall.confirmExplain: Confirm receipt and release payment to the seller? This transaction costs gas. After confirmation this order cannot be refunded.

sales.title: Direct sales
sales.notice: Direct-sales mode: payment goes straight to the seller in the same transaction (10% platform fee) — there is no escrow and NO platform refund. Delivery is manual: the seller delivers the file key when online. Buying grants the file itself (no DRM). Only encrypted files make sense to sell. Rate honestly: up/down votes are on-chain (gas applies), one vote per buyer per product, changeable.

sales.selectHint: Listing or re-pricing creates a new immutable revision; sold orders are never affected.
